newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says no change in EMU policy.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says no change in EMU policy.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday there was no change in his Conservative party's policy over a single European currency.

Asked about reports that he had said in a BBC television interview that British membership of European economic and monetary union "certainly isn't going to be in this parliament". Major said, if he had said that, it was a slip of the tongue.

"I'm not sure you've got it in context. What I was seeking to say to people was that I think it is very unlikely that the economic circumstances will be ready for 1999," Major told his final news conference of the election campaign.
"I don't have the transcript in front of me. But there was no intention to change policy and I don't think I did," Major said. "If I said it, it was a slip of the tongue."
Major's government has kept the option open of joining EMU in January 1999.
Election day is just one day away with latest opinion polls showing the opposition Labour Party 18 percentage points ahead.
